F1 ILCA 2026: the labels the notice board posted (QP/QE), and a discard that may fall in either stage

ILCA 6 2026 — ILCA 6 Women's World Championship, Dun Laoghaire IRL · F1 · SI (reference-docs:events/ilca6-women-worlds-2026/SI-with-Amendment-4.md) · results

2 qualifying fleets · → Gold/Silver · discards: 1 discard from race 3, 2 discards from race 10.
What a championship calls its races is the event's decision, not the class's.
These sailing instructions number the Preliminary and Elimination series in
one sequence — SI 18.4's discard table is keyed to it, "Q1-Q2 … Q3-Q9 …
Q10-Q12" — and the event posted QP1–QP5 then QE1 onward instead. The men's
Worlds, two weeks earlier under the same instructions, posted Q1–Q5 then
E1–E7. So this fixture carries `raceLabels`, and its preview column headings
are the ones on the real published page.

The labels change no arithmetic: the discard ladder counts races, and at 9
races the real event allowed one discard exactly as SI 18.4's Q3-Q9 row
says. Real Dun Laoghaire was 2 fleets of ~54 (Gold/Yellow and Silver/Blue in
the published tables), 5 Preliminary races then 4 Elimination races at the
point this was captured, one discard, DNC = largest Preliminary fleet + 1.
Reduced here to 2 fleets of 3 over QP1-QP3 + QE1-QE2, so the single discard
is unlocked (ILCA's 2026 ladder opens it at 3 races) and every cell is
checkable by hand.

Two things worth reading off the table. The discard may land in either
stage: y1 and b1 each drop an Elimination score, which SI 18.4 permits
because two Elimination races were completed and at most one may be
excluded. And where a boat's worst score is tied — b2 scored 3 in both QP3
and QE1 — the earlier race is the one excluded (RRS A2.1), so her discard
stays in the Preliminary series. `expected` verified against the engine.
